questions.question: Where can users access the Visualization Designer in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations

explanation.correct: If you need custom charts, go to All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations, or use the Column Context menus and lists to create charts directly from the data. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User Administration handles users and roles, not visualizations.
System Security manages access controls, not reporting.
While Incident has reports, the Visualization Designer is in Platform Analytics.

source.excerpt: If you need custom charts, go to All, Platform Analytics, Library, Data Visualizations, or use the Column Context menus and lists to create charts directly from the data.

questions.question: What is the recommended best practice when creating a new visualization in ServiceNow?

options.text: Duplicate an existing visualization and edit your copy
Use only the default system visualizations

explanation.correct: It's often easier to build charts starting from a filtered list or existing visualization, where configuration options are pre-provided. It's best practice to duplicate an existing visualization, and then edit your copy to fit your needs. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Starting from scratch is less efficient; duplicating saves time.
ServiceNow has built-in visualization tools; importing external tools adds complexity.
Custom visualizations are often needed to meet specific business requirements.

source.excerpt: It's often easier to build charts starting from a filtered list or existing visualization, where configuration options are pre-provided. It's best practice to duplicate an existing visualization, and then edit your copy to fit your needs.

questions.question: What is the key difference between one-time reporting and Performance Analytics?

options.text: Performance Analytics shows trends over time; one-time reporting shows where you are today
Performance Analytics only works with incident data

explanation.correct: One-time reporting shows 'where are we today?' while Performance Analytics reveals trends over time. PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both provide accurate data; they serve different purposes.
Performance Analytics typically requires additional licensing, not one-time reporting.
PA works with data across the platform, not just incidents.

source.excerpt: One-time reporting shows, where are we today? While performance analytics reveals trends over time.

questions.question: Which visualization types are available in ServiceNow? (Choose two)

explanation.correct: ServiceNow offers various visualization types including speedometer, dial, single score, pie, semi-donut, bubble, and text analytics. Gantt charts and 3D surface plots are not standard visualization types. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Gantt charts are specialized project management visualizations, not standard in the Visualization Designer.
3D surface plots are not included in ServiceNow's standard visualization options.

source.excerpt: Other visualization types include speedometer, dial, single score, pie, semi-donut, bubble, and text analytics.

questions.question: What are the two types of dashboards in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: Dashboards can be responsive or non-responsive. Non-responsive dashboards have limits on who can create, view, and edit them. Responsive dashboards adapt to different screen sizes. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: While dashboards have sharing options, the types are responsive vs non-responsive.
Static and dynamic describe data updates, not dashboard architecture types.
Basic and advanced are not the official dashboard type classifications.

source.excerpt: Dashboards can be responsive or non-responsive. Non-responsive dashboards have limits on who can create, view, and edit them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Data' configuration option in the Visualization Designer?

options.text: To set the visualization's color scheme
To choose where your data comes from - a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table
To export the visualization to PDF

explanation.correct: The Data configuration option lets you choose where your data comes from - either a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table. This is fundamental to building any visualization. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Color scheme is set in the Presentation configuration option.
Exporting is a separate action, not a configuration option.
Scheduling is handled through different settings.

source.excerpt: Data, choose where your data comes from, either a predefined data source or a ServiceNow table.

questions.question: How can a user add a visualization to a dashboard in ServiceNow?

options.text: Only by creating the dashboard first
Only by using the import function
By creating a dashboard first and adding the visualization, or by saving the visualization and selecting 'Add to Dashboard'
Visualizations cannot be added to dashboards

explanation.correct: To add a visualization to a dashboard, either create a dashboard first and add the visualization as an element, or save the visualization and select 'Add to Dashboard' for a new or existing dashboard. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: You can also add from the visualization side using 'Add to Dashboard'.
Import is not required; native options allow adding visualizations to dashboards.
Adding visualizations to dashboards is a core feature of Platform Analytics.

source.excerpt: To add a visualization to a dashboard, either create a dashboard first and add the visualization as an element, or save the visualization and select Add to Dashboard for a new or existing dashboard.

questions.question: What does Performance Analytics capture to show accurate historical trends?

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions. Unlike one-time reporting, PA development is ongoing and can be refined over time. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Login records are captured in system logs, not PA snapshots.
Email notifications are part of communication, not PA data collection.
Configuration changes are tracked in update sets, not PA snapshots.

source.excerpt: PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions.

questions.question: What does the 'Type' configuration option in the Visualization Designer allow you to do?

options.text: Select the data table to use
Choose from over 20 chart types for your visualization

explanation.correct: The Type configuration option lets you pick from over 20 chart types for your visualization, including bar charts, pie charts, speedometers, and more. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data source selection is done in the 'Data' configuration option.
Permissions are managed through sharing and roles, not the Type option.
Email recipients are configured for scheduled reports, not visualization type.

source.excerpt: Type, pick from over 20 chart types for your visualization.

questions.question: What does the 'Presentation' configuration option in the Visualization Designer control?

options.text: Which users can view the visualization
Appearance customization including color, titles, and legend adjustments

explanation.correct: The Presentation configuration option allows you to customize the appearance, including color, titles, and legend adjustments. This controls how the visualization looks to users. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User access is controlled through sharing options and permissions.
Data grouping and calculations are set in the 'Group By and Sorting' option.
Scheduling is a separate function for automated report distribution.

source.excerpt: Presentation, customize the appearance, including color, titles, and legend adjustments.

questions.question: A manager wants to track incident resolution trends over the past year. Which ServiceNow feature should they use?

explanation.correct: Performance Analytics reveals trends over time and captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends. For tracking resolution trends over a year, PA provides the trending capabilities needed for this analysis. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: List views show current data but don't provide trend analysis over time.
Knowledge Base stores articles, not analytics or trending data.
Service Catalog is for requesting services, not reporting.

source.excerpt: Performance analytics reveals trends over time... PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends.

questions.question: Where can users access Analytics Center in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: To access data visualizations and dashboards, go to All > Platform Analytics > Analytics Center. You can choose to create a new dashboard or a new visualization from there. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Definition is for system records and scripts, not analytics.
This path doesn't exist; Analytics Center is under Platform Analytics.
System Administration handles system settings, not analytics.

source.excerpt: To access data visualizations and dashboards, go to All, Platform Analytics, Analytics Center.

questions.question: What can ServiceNow visualizations be used for? (Choose two)

options.text: Shown as bar charts, pie charts, and other chart types

explanation.correct: Visualizations can be shown as bar charts, pie charts, etc., and can be run manually or automatically scheduled. They include conditions for features like incident management and service catalog requests, including KPI reports. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=116f675847b35ad4ca332a81736d438d&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Visualizations display data; they don't directly modify database records.
Security controls are managed separately and are not replaced by visualizations.

source.excerpt: Visualizations can be shown as bar charts, pie charts, et cetera, and can be run manually or automatically scheduled.

questions.question: Where can you access the collection of data visualizations in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations

explanation.correct: Navigate to All > Platform Analytics > Library > Data Visualizations to access the collection of visualizations. You can use these to create custom visuals.

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Definition is for tables and scripts, not visualizations.
This is not the correct navigation path for data visualizations.
System UI is for UI components, not analytics visualizations.

questions.question: What is the recommended best practice when creating a new visualization?

options.text: Always start from scratch for maximum customization
Duplicate an existing visualization and edit the copy to fit your needs
Import visualization templates from the ServiceNow Store
Use only the default visualizations provided by ServiceNow

explanation.correct: It's best practice to duplicate an existing visualization, then edit your copy to fit your needs. It's often easier to build charts starting from a filtered list or existing visualization where configuration options are pre-provided.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Starting from scratch is more time-consuming; duplicating an existing visualization is recommended.
While templates exist, the recommended approach is to duplicate existing visualizations.
Customization is encouraged; you're not limited to default visualizations.

questions.question: What is the key difference between one-time reporting and Performance Analytics?

options.text: One-time reporting is more accurate than Performance Analytics
One-time reporting shows current state; Performance Analytics reveals trends over time
Performance Analytics only works with incident data
One-time reporting requires a separate license

explanation.correct: One-time reporting shows 'where are we today?' while Performance Analytics reveals trends over time. PA captures regular snapshots to show accurate historical trends, helping to review indicators, monitor metrics, and improve decisions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both provide accurate data; the difference is point-in-time vs. trending over time.
Performance Analytics works with any ServiceNow data, not just incidents.

questions.question: How do you add a visualization to a dashboard in ServiceNow?

options.text: Drag and drop from the visualization library only
Either create a dashboard first and add visualizations, or save a visualization and select 'Add to Dashboard'
Visualizations are automatically added to the default dashboard
Export the visualization and import it into the dashboard

explanation.correct: You can either create a dashboard first and add the visualization as an element, or save the visualization and select 'Add to Dashboard' for a new or existing dashboard.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While drag and drop is available, you can also use 'Add to Dashboard' from a saved visualization.
Visualizations are not automatically added to any dashboard.
There is no export/import process needed — you can add directly.

questions.question: Which configuration options are available in the Visualization Designer? (Choose 2)

options.text: Data source selection (predefined or ServiceNow table)

explanation.correct: In the Visualization Designer, you can choose where your data comes from (predefined data source or ServiceNow table) and pick from over 20 chart types. Other options include Group By/Sorting and Presentation customization.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Email scheduling is configured separately, not directly in the Visualization Designer.
The Visualization Designer works within ServiceNow, not with external BI tools.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Gantt charts are not listed among the standard ServiceNow visualization types.
Waterfall charts are not listed among the standard ServiceNow visualization types.

questions.question: What are the two types of dashboards in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: Dashboards can be responsive or non-responsive. Non-responsive dashboards have limits on who can create, view, and edit them.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The classification is responsive vs non-responsive, not static vs dynamic.
While dashboards can be shared, the types are responsive and non-responsive.
The types are responsive and non-responsive, not basic and advanced.

questions.question: A manager wants a dashboard that shows real-time incident counts by priority, updated every 5 minutes. Which report type should the administrator create?

options.text: A bar chart report on the Incident table grouped by Priority with auto-refresh enabled on the dashboard
A scheduled PDF export sent every 5 minutes
A static HTML page with hardcoded data
A Performance Analytics indicator with real-time collection

explanation.correct: A standard report (bar chart grouped by Priority) added to a dashboard with auto-refresh enabled provides near-real-time data. Dashboard auto-refresh intervals can be configured to update at regular intervals.

wrongAnswers.explanation: PDF exports are static snapshots sent via email; they don't provide a real-time dashboard view.
Static HTML pages don't connect to live data and require manual updates.
Performance Analytics collects data at scheduled intervals (daily by default) and isn't designed for 5-minute real-time counts. Standard reports are more appropriate for this.

questions.question: Which two report types are available in ServiceNow's Report Designer? (Choose 2)

explanation.correct: Pie charts and Pivot tables are both standard report types available in ServiceNow's Report Designer. Other available types include bar charts, line charts, donut charts, and trend reports.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Gantt charts are used in Project Management but are not a standard Report Designer type.
3D scatter plots are not available in ServiceNow's reporting tools.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'Report' and a 'Performance Analytics (PA) Dashboard' in ServiceNow?

options.text: Reports show current data snapshots; PA Dashboards show trends over time using collected indicator data
Reports are for managers; PA Dashboards are for administrators only
They show the same data in different formats
Reports are deprecated in favor of PA Dashboards

explanation.correct: Standard Reports query live data for point-in-time snapshots. Performance Analytics collects and stores indicator data over time, enabling trend analysis, comparisons, and historical insights that standard reports cannot provide.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both Reports and PA Dashboards can be shared with any user who has appropriate access.
They serve different purposes — PA provides historical trends while Reports provide current-state views.
Standard Reports remain fully supported and are complementary to PA.

questions.question: An administrator creates a report but a user in the 'itil' group cannot see it on their dashboard. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The report has not been shared with the user's group or role
The user's browser doesn't support reports
Reports can only be viewed by the creator

explanation.correct: Reports must be explicitly shared with users, groups, or roles to be visible on their dashboards. By default, a report is only visible to its creator until sharing permissions are configured.

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow reports work in all modern browsers; browser compatibility is not the issue.
Reports CAN be shared with other users through the sharing settings.
Auto-refresh affects data currency, not report visibility.

questions.question: What is a 'scheduled report' in ServiceNow?

options.text: A report that is automatically generated and distributed via email at configured intervals
A report that can only be run during business hours
A report that requires manual approval before each run
A report that deletes itself after a set period

explanation.correct: Scheduled reports run automatically at configured intervals (daily, weekly, monthly) and distribute the results via email to specified recipients as PDF or other formats.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Scheduled reports can run at any time, not just during business hours.
Scheduled reports run automatically without requiring approval for each execution.
Reports persist until manually deleted; they don't auto-expire.

questions.question: Which feature allows users to interact with report data by clicking on chart elements to drill down into the underlying records?

options.text: Report drilldown — clicking a chart segment opens the filtered list of records
Report scheduling — scheduled reports include drill-down links
Report export — exporting to PDF enables interactive drill-down
Report cloning — creating copies enables different views

explanation.correct: ServiceNow reports support interactive drilldown — clicking on a bar, pie slice, or other chart element opens a filtered list showing the individual records that make up that data point.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Scheduled reports are static exports; they don't support interactive drill-down.
PDF exports are static documents without interactive capabilities.
Cloning creates separate report copies; it doesn't enable drill-down.
